children: The Manheim Used Vehicle Value Index, a widely followed gauge of wholesale used-vehicle prices in the US, fell 0.9% month-on-month in August 2026, marking a second consecutive monthly decline.
On a yearly basis, price growth slowed to 0.4%, the weakest pace since December 2025, as resilience in EV and compact-car prices was offset by continued declines in pickups and SUVs.
Cox Automotive Chief Economist Jeremy Robb said depreciation was stronger in July and early August before easing toward the end of the month.

While younger vehicle cohorts saw greater depreciation, older and more affordable cars held up better, with nine- and 10-year-old vehicles remaining about six percentage points above their long-term averages, underscoring steady demand for affordable used cars.
Used retail sales continued to strengthen through August, while retail days’ supply fell to 44 days from 46 at the end of July.
Stronger demand and tighter supply continued to support dealer purchases from Manheim.

title: US Used-Car Prices Fall for Second Month
